parts.visual:
A founder gives an incredibly charismatic presentation. The slides are beautiful. The vision is massive. The investor looks at the final slide and says: 'But you have zero users.' The pitch is dead.

The Evidence:
1. Traction is quantitative evidence of market demand. It proves that you are not just a dreamer; you are an executor.
2. Traction is a graph that goes up and to the right. It can be Revenue, Active Users, or signed Letters of Intent (LOIs). It is the most important slide in any Pitch Deck.
parts.audio: Ideas are cheap; execution is everything. Investors do not fund ideas. They fund Traction. The Traction slide proves that strangers are actually using or paying for your product.

questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest form of 'Traction' for an early-stage SaaS startup?
options: $10,000 in Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) from 100 unaffiliated, paying customers with a 2% churn rate.
questions.correct_answer: $10,000 in Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) from 100 unaffiliated, paying customers with a 2% churn rate.
questions.explanation: Cash from strangers is the ultimate proof of value.

questions.question: Listen to the founder. Why is the VC completely unimpressed by their 'Traction'?
questions.tts_text: We have amazing traction! We have 5,000 total registered users. Sure, nobody has actually logged in for three months, but the total number looks huge on the graph!
options: The founder is using a 'Vanity Metric' (Total Registered Users). Investors only care about 'Active Metrics' (Daily Active Users). A user who creates an account and never returns is a failure, not traction.
questions.correct_answer: The founder is using a 'Vanity Metric' (Total Registered Users). Investors only care about 'Active Metrics' (Daily Active Users). A user who creates an account and never returns is a failure, not traction.
questions.explanation: Vanity metrics make you look good. Actionable metrics help you make decisions.

questions.question: If a B2B startup is 'Pre-Revenue' (they haven't finished building the software yet), how can they still show Traction to an investor?
options: By showing signed Letters of Intent (LOIs) from major corporations stating: 'If you build this exact software, we agree to buy it for $50,000.'
By showing their high school grades.
questions.correct_answer: By showing signed Letters of Intent (LOIs) from major corporations stating: 'If you build this exact software, we agree to buy it for $50,000.'
questions.explanation: An LOI is a legal precursor to a contract and serves as powerful validation.

questions.question: What is 'MoM Growth' and why do VCs obsess over it on the Traction slide?
options: Month-over-Month Growth. VCs want to see a compounding growth rate (e.g., growing revenue by 10% every single month). The slope of the line proves the startup is scaling.
questions.correct_answer: Month-over-Month Growth. VCs want to see a compounding growth rate (e.g., growing revenue by 10% every single month). The slope of the line proves the startup is scaling.
questions.explanation: 10% monthly growth turns $1,000 into $3,000 in a year. Compounding is magic.
